note: Every chapter is one headline and one sentence. Values in {braces} are filled from the data files at run time.

mars.title: Your first walk on Mars.
mars.line: Six missions mapped this ground before you arrived. REDCAIRN turns what they saw into a guide you can walk.

crater.title: A mountain inside a crater.
crater.line: Gale is 154 km across. Mount Sharp rises {mountainKm} km from its floor. You will walk on its lower slopes.

water.title: Orbiters saw water here first.
water.line: Blue dots: minerals that only form in water, found from orbit by CRISM and OMEGA. That is why we came.

rover.title: A rover tested the ground for you.
rover.line: Curiosity drove {roverKm} km and climbed {roverClimb} m in fourteen years. The white end of its line is your walk.

walk.title: 1.5 km out. Five stops. Home with air to spare.
walk.line: Green ground is safe in a suit, amber needs care, red is too steep. The route is the rover's own track.

storm.title: The Sun just flared.
storm.line: REDCAIRN redraws the way home: {directMin} instead of {trailMin}, with {less}% less radiation. No hill here blocks more than {shelter}%. Go now.

home.title: Home, with {airLeft} of air.
home.line: Curiosity is still out there, {roverAheadM} m past your turnaround, climbing. It walked this ground alone so that you would not have to.

objective: Today: walk {walkKm} km of Perseverance’s first tracks, from where it landed to the first rock it kept, and be home with air to spare.

DOCK.title: The hatch
DOCK.moment: You are standing where it landed.
DOCK.sub: Perseverance touched down here on 18 February 2021, after seven minutes of falling. The team named the place Octavia E. Butler Landing. Its first tracks lead south. Follow them.

WP1.title: The overlook
WP1.moment: From here, it watched something fly.
WP1.sub: 19 April 2021. Perseverance parked on this spot and turned its cameras east. Ingenuity, a 1.8 kg helicopter carrying a scrap of the Wright brothers’ 1903 Flyer, rose three metres and hovered for 39 seconds. It went on to fly 72 times.

WP2.title: Máaz
WP2.moment: They expected lake mud. They found lava.
WP2.sub: The floor of Jezero turned out to be volcanic rock, later touched by water. The team named it Máaz, the Navajo word for Mars. Your suit’s slope limit is 20°; here the ground barely tilts.

WP3.title: Roubion
WP3.moment: Its first try came up empty.
WP3.sub: 6 August 2021. The drill went in, the rock crumbled, and the tube sealed with nothing but Martian air. The team kept it anyway: the first sample of another planet’s air waiting to come home. Purple ground on the map hides part of the sky.

PERSEVERANCE.title: Rochette
PERSEVERANCE.moment: Here it kept its first piece of Mars.
PERSEVERANCE.sub: September 2021. Two cores from this ridge, Montdenier and Montagnac, sealed in tubes: the first rock from another planet set aside to be brought home. Perseverance has moved on; today it is far up the crater rim, still driving.

radio._note: Lines heard on the suit radio, one at a time. 'real' lines are quoted from the source named; every other line is imagined and says so on screen. 'audio' is played through the radio filter if the file exists.

plan.text: Habitat to EVA-1 and EVA-2: route uploaded. Pick your line.

stop-0.text: Habitat to EVA-1, EVA-2: you are clear. Follow its tracks.

stop-3.text: Turnaround. Leave something for whoever comes next.

home.text: Both suits at the hatch. Welcome home, {name}.

intro.title: Jezero crater: where Perseverance landed.
intro.body: This is the second walk, built by the same scripts from Jezero’s own maps: the 1 m elevation model and 25 cm photo Perseverance used to land, and the track it drove. The orange line is Perseverance, {roverKm} km in {latestSol} sols. Your walk follows its first {walkKm} km, from where it landed to the first rock it kept.

storm.body: You and EVA-2 are at Rochette, {walkKm} km from the hatch. The real solar storm of September 2017 is replayed here, as Curiosity measured it at Gale (Perseverance carries no particle-radiation detector). The map has drawn three ways back on Jezero’s real terrain.

home.title: It came here to leave something for us.
home.body: You walked {walkKm} km of the first tracks Perseverance made, to the first rock it kept for Earth, and came home. That tube is still waiting to be collected.{mine}

roverStop.kicker: Rochette · sol {sol} · the first rock cores
roverStop.win: Where Perseverance stood on sol {sol}, drilling its first cores. Our rover model marks the spot; the real rover has moved on. Drag to look around.

cards.homeWin: From the hatch, looking back along its tracks.
